commands.review_summary:
The branch adds transient EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK/EINTR retry and fail-closed preservation for session write-lock cleanup, plus two focused regression tests.

PR surface: Source +54, Tests +81. Total +135 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-level. Current main collapses cleanup read failures to a null payload, and an old null-payload lock can pass the mtime stale-removal path; I did not run a live gateway or doctor repro.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Needs contributor real-behavior proof, maintainer acceptance of the fail-closed availability tradeoff, and a small diagnostic follow-up; proof remains a human-only merge gate.

target.title: fix(agents): retry transient reads and fail closed when sweeping stale session write locks
target.body:
Related: #100910

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the gateway's startup session-lock sweep (and
`openclaw doctor`) can delete a valid, actively-held session write lock, breaking
mutual exclusion on a session's transcript. When cleanup reads a lock file, any
transient filesystem error (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK/EINTR under load) is collapsed to
a "no payload" result, which reads as a missing PID. Past the 30-second mtime
grace the lock is then removed with no content-identity check — so a transient
read on a live lock (held for up to the 5-minute max hold) deletes it, after
which a second writer can acquire a fresh lock while the original holder is still
writing the same JSONL.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup removal decision (`cleanStaleLockFiles`) now reads each lock through
`readLockPayloadForCleanup`, which (1) retries only transient read errors — the
same `{EAGAIN, EWOULDBLOCK, EINTR}` classifier used for workspace bootstrap reads
in #100910 — and (2) **fails closed**: if the read still cannot complete after
retries, the lock is reported as unreadable and left in place rather than
removed. A malformed/empty but readable lock is still a successful read (payload
null, reclaimable once old), so existing stale-reclaim behavior is unchanged.
This is scoped to the cleanup removal decision only: the fs-safe **acquire** path
already throws on these transient codes and guards stale removal with a
content-identity re-check, so it needs no change, and the acquire-timeout
diagnostics readers are intentionally left as simple non-retrying reads.

## User Impact

Operators no longer risk a transient IO blip (a single spike or a short burst)
during gateway startup or `openclaw doctor` silently deleting a live session lock
and letting two writers race on the same transcript. No API, config, or
success-path behavior change; readable malformed locks are still reclaimed once
old.

## Evidence

Two focused regression tests run `cleanStaleLockFiles` against a valid, live
OpenClaw-owned lock aged past the grace (the `readOwnerProcessArgs: () =>
["openclaw"]` injection models an OpenClaw-owned holder so the test-runner argv
is not classified as a foreign owner), while injecting transient `EAGAIN` reads:

```
 ✓ retries a transient read during cleanup so a live lock is not wrongly removed
     // single blip → retry recovers the payload → lock preserved
 ✓ does not remove a live lock when transient reads exhaust retries during cleanup
     // sustained burst → all retries fail → fail closed → lock preserved

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  56 passed (56)
```

Negative control — reverting the fix fails exactly these two tests, confirming
they exercise both the retry and the fail-closed path (the null payload otherwise
falls into the mtime grace and is removed):

```
 × retries a transient read during cleanup so a live lock is not wrongly removed
 × does not remove a live lock when transient reads exhaust retries during cleanup
      Tests  2 failed | 54 passed (56)
```

Run locally with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts`;
full changed-lane checks are delegated to CI.
